sentences.en: A diamond.
sentences.zh: 一颗钻石。

sentences.en: I studied economics as an undergraduate, and one thing they tell you as an economics major is
sentences.zh: 我读本科时学的是经济学，经济学专业告诉你的一点是

sentences.en: that people are rational.
sentences.zh: 人们是理性的。

sentences.en: But as far as Nero could tell, there was nothing particularly rational about
sentences.zh: 但在妮鲁看来，买钻石这件事

sentences.en: buying a diamond.
sentences.zh: 并没有什么特别理性可言。

sentences.en: Now, you can argue that diamonds are beautiful, but there are cheaper stones that
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以说钻石很美，但也有更便宜的石头

sentences.en: are just as pretty.
sentences.zh: 同样漂亮。

sentences.en: So then the question is, why are people spending so much money on these shiny
sentences.zh: 所以问题就在于，为什么人们要花这么多钱买这些没有内在价值的

sentences.en: rocks that have no intrinsic value?
sentences.zh: 闪亮石头？

sentences.en: And you know, there's effectively a perfect substitute.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，实际上存在完美的替代品。

sentences.en: And then
sentences.zh: 然后

sentences.en: it seemed like it was all this kind of psychological stuff that people wanted to express their status.
sentences.zh: 这似乎全是那种人们想要表达自己地位的心理把戏。

sentences.en: People wanted to kind of fit in with sort of the normative practices in terms of marriage.
sentences.zh: 人们希望融入某种关于婚姻的规范化做法中。

sentences.en: And it's just sort of dawned on me that products have all this psychological value, and that's worth real money.
sentences.zh: 我突然意识到，产品蕴含着各种心理价值，而这确实价值不菲。

sentences.en: I mean, a whole industry is based on just sort of pure kind of signaling and psychological value.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个行业仅仅建立在纯粹的表征和心理价值之上。

sentences.en: And I found that to be really interesting and sort of at odds with this notion that people are rational.
sentences.zh: 我发现这非常有趣，而且与“人们是理性的”这一观点相矛盾。

sentences.en: This idea made Nero, who's now a marketing professor at Georgetown University,
sentences.zh: 这个想法让现在担任乔治敦大学市场营销教授的妮鲁

sentences.en: think about the other ways we use money as a signaling device to express our beliefs and our values.
sentences.zh: 开始思考我们用金钱作为表征工具来表达信仰和价值观的其他方式。

sentences.en: We enact our political will usually by voting or supporting different kinds of legislations and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我们通常通过投票、支持各种立法之类的事情来行使我们的政治意志。

sentences.en: So it's kind of interesting when people start taking that civic actions, these kind of civic actions into the market,
sentences.zh: 所以，当人们开始把这种公民行动、这类公民行动带入市场时，这就变得挺有趣的了

sentences.en: and then start boycotting or boycotting a certain brand or a certain company
sentences.zh: 然后开始抵制或联合抵制某个品牌或某家公司

sentences.en: in order to express their view.
sentences.zh: 以表达他们的观点。

sentences.en: And you can kind of think about it in terms of what ends up being more tangible.
sentences.zh: 你可以从什么最终更具象的角度来思考这个问题。

sentences.en: So if we think about voting, it's sort of an abstract process.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们考虑投票，这算是一个抽象的过程。

sentences.en: It's not very public.
sentences.zh: 它不是非常公开。

sentences.en: Whereas when you buy a product or avoid buying a product, it's very tangible.
sentences.zh: 然而，当你购买某件产品或避免购买某件产品时，它是非常具象的。

sentences.en: If you're someone who doesn't buy flashy jewelry, you may say,
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个不买浮华珠宝的人，你可能会说：

sentences.en: OK, I'm not one of those people who uses money to talk.
sentences.zh: “好吧，我不是那种用金钱说话的人。”

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: Or maybe you just don't use diamonds to talk.
sentences.zh: 或者可能你只是不用钻石来表达。

sentences.en: You use coffee.
sentences.zh: 你用咖啡。

sentences.en: I've studied the situations between small coffee shops and large coffee shops.
sentences.zh: 我研究过小型咖啡馆和大型咖啡馆之间的情况。

sentences.en: And so I have a paper where we show that for a small coffee shop, if it's just sitting there by itself,
sentences.zh: 我有一篇论文展示了，对于一家独立的小咖啡馆来说，如果它就孤零零地呆在那里，

sentences.en: people don't really think much of the political situation.
sentences.zh: 人们其实并不会过多地去想政治情况。

sentences.en: They just think more about the coffee, sort of about the more rational economic features and attributes of the product.
sentences.zh: 他们更多地考虑咖啡，也就是产品更具理性的经济特征和属性。

sentences.en: But as soon as you put a large competitor in next door, say you put a Starbucks in next door, all of a sudden it becomes this fight between the little guy and the big guy.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你在隔壁放一个大型竞争对手，比如在隔壁开一家星巴克，它突然就变成了小人物和大人物之间的斗争。

sentences.en: And then buying your cup of coffee is really meaningful.
sentences.zh: 然后你买的那杯咖啡就真的变得很有意义了。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, it's a symbol of what you believe in.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，它成了你信仰的象征。

sentences.en: It's a symbol of you supporting the little guy, of you supporting the underdog and trying to stick it to the man.
sentences.zh: 它成了你支持小人物、支持弱者并试图对抗强权的象征。

sentences.en: And it's so tangible.
sentences.zh: 而且它是如此具象。

sentences.en: And I just find it so fascinating that that's sort of how we kind of we kind of express our political views on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这太迷人了，这就是我们日常表达政治观点的方式。

sentences.en: And we feel, you know, powerful in a sense that we actually sort of have a say in this situation.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在某种意义上感到很有力量，觉得自己在这个局势中确实有发言权。

sentences.en: Companies, of course, pay attention to what consumers want.
sentences.zh: 当然，公司会关注消费者的需求。

sentences.en: They understand that people don't just want to buy a cup of coffee or a computer.
sentences.zh: 他们明白，人们不仅仅想买一杯咖啡或一台电脑。

sentences.en: They want the right story to go with that cup of coffee or computer.
sentences.zh: 他们希望那杯咖啡或那台电脑能配上一个合适的故事。

sentences.en: This is why so many Silicon Valley companies that are worth billions of dollars
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么那么多价值数十亿美元的硅谷公司

sentences.en: spend so much time telling us about their origin stories,
sentences.zh: 花那么多时间向我们讲述他们的起源故事，

sentences.en: how two kids dropped out of college to explore a dream in someone's garage.
sentences.zh: 讲述两个辍学生如何在某个车库里追逐梦想。

sentences.en: So this is what we call, we have another paper around underdog brand biographies,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们所说的——我们还有另一篇关于弱者品牌传记的论文——

sentences.en: and this sort of idea of kind of starting in a garage from humble beginnings,
sentences.zh: 这种从车库起步、出身卑微的想法，

sentences.en: but overcoming obstacles to kind of fulfill your dream.
sentences.zh: 但克服重重障碍去实现你的梦想。

sentences.en: That's a really compelling narrative, especially to Americans.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常引人入胜的故事，尤其是对美国人而言。

sentences.en: I think because of the whole kind of pull yourself up from your bootstraps and this whole notion of the American dream.
sentences.zh: 我想这是因为“靠自己的力量站起来”这种整体文化以及美国梦的整个概念。

sentences.en: And so companies that take advantage of that narrative and if they use it effectively, even as they grow, can kind of remind consumers that, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，利用这种叙事并在不断发展的过程中有效运用它的公司，可以提醒消费者：

sentences.en: this was a small company and they might, you know, identify with it more and thus, you know, like penalize them less for being a large company.
sentences.zh: 这曾是一家小公司，他们可能会（你知道的）对它更有认同感，因此（你知道的）对他们作为一家大公司的惩罚就会少一些。

sentences.en: There tends to be sort of a kind of an aversion or a disdain for large companies.
sentences.zh: 人们往往对大公司有一种厌恶或蔑视的情绪。

sentences.en: people tend to identify a lot more with smaller companies.
sentences.zh: 人们往往对小公司更有认同感。

sentences.en: And you tell the story of Nantucket Nectars, which also has the same sort of startup story.
sentences.zh: 你讲了楠塔基特花蜜的故事，它也有着类似的创业故事。

sentences.en: A lot of companies, they talk about how Nantucket Nectars in particular
sentences.zh: 许多公司都在谈论，尤其是楠塔基特花蜜公司

sentences.en: talks about how they started with a blender and a dream.
sentences.zh: 讲述他们如何凭借一个搅拌机和一个梦想起家。

sentences.en: And Cliff Bar talks about how, you know, they started in their garage with,
sentences.zh: 克利夫酒吧则谈到他们如何在车库里起步，

sentences.en: he was living with his dog and his skis and, you know, was cooking.
sentences.zh: 当时他跟他的狗和滑雪板住在一起，并且（你知道的）还在做饭。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's a sort of underdog narrative that makes use of this sort of external disadvantage, but really, you know, trying hard.
sentences.zh: 而且，（你知道的）这是一种弱者叙事，利用了这种外部劣势，但确实（你知道的）在努力拼搏。

sentences.en: And I think people really, really find that story resonating because I think we all on some level feel like underdogs.
sentences.zh: 我想人们真的非常、非常喜欢这个故事，因为我认为我们在某种程度上都觉得自己是弱者。

sentences.en: And so it sort of is can be motivating to us.
sentences.zh: 所以它对我们来说可以起到激励作用。

sentences.en: Of course, the underdog is not the only type of brand that can draw us in.
sentences.zh: 当然，弱者并不是唯一能吸引我们的品牌类型。

sentences.en: In fact, Nero has found that brands that are powerful, brands that might be seen as the opposite of the underdog, can also attract people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，妮鲁发现，强大的品牌、那些可能被视为弱者反面的品牌，也能吸引人。

sentences.en: One example, Walmart.
sentences.zh: 一个例子是沃尔玛。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: So there's this relationship between status and power.
sentences.zh: 地位和权力之间存在着这样一种关系。

sentences.en: And so status is a way, is sort of what we get when we have power.
sentences.zh: 地位是一种方式，也就是我们拥有权力时所获得的某种东西。

sentences.en: And so when we think about power, we can think about Walmart as being a really powerful brand.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们想到权力时，我们可以认为沃尔玛是一个非常强大的品牌。

sentences.en: It has a lot of strength in the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 它在市场上有很强的实力。

sentences.en: And so that strength, that kind of access to power, having a lot of resources as a brand in itself,
sentences.zh: 因此，这种实力，这种获得权力的途径，作为品牌本身拥有大量资源，

sentences.en: Even though it's kind of a low-end brand, if you compare it to other low-end brands, that can be kind of attractive to people who care about status.
sentences.zh: 尽管它某种程度上算是一个低端品牌，如果你把它和其他低端品牌相比，这对关心地位的人来说还是很有吸引力的。

sentences.en: Many of us understand the economic choices we make can have real ethical consequences.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都明白，我们做出的经济选择会产生真实的道德后果。

sentences.en: The products we buy can adversely affect the environment or take advantage of poor people in distant countries.
sentences.zh: 我们购买的产品可能会对环境产生负面影响，或者剥削遥远国家的穷人。

sentences.en: We can buy stuff from stores that treat employees well, or we can buy things sometimes at a cheaper price from stores that treat their employees poorly.
sentences.zh: 我们可以从善待员工的商店买东西，或者有时从虐待员工的商店以更便宜的价格买东西。

sentences.en: Often, after a big news story about conditions in sweatshops or the use of child labor, there's public outrage.
sentences.zh: 通常，在关于血汗工厂环境或使用童工的大新闻报道之后，会出现公众的愤怒。

sentences.en: But as Nero has explored, our actions don't always match our rhetoric.
sentences.zh: 但正如妮鲁所探究的那样，我们的行动并不总是与我们的言论相符。

sentences.en: She once wrote a paper on the subject titled, Sweatshop Labor is Wrong Unless the Shoes Are Cute.
sentences.zh: 她曾写过一篇以此为主题的论文，名为《血汗工厂的劳工是错误的，除非鞋子很可爱》。

sentences.en: The idea there is that you kind of decide how much you like something, and so you really like a pair of shoes.
sentences.zh: 那里的核心想法是，你先决定自己有多喜欢某样东西，比如你真的很喜欢一双鞋。

sentences.en: And so then kind of the moral reasoning starts from there.
sentences.zh: 然后，道德推理就从这里开始了。

sentences.en: It doesn't start from kind of a neutral place where you're like, where you say, oh, sweatshop labor is wrong.
sentences.zh: 它不是从一个中立的立场开始的，比如你说，哦，血汗工厂的劳工是错误的。

sentences.en: You know, under any circumstances, I don't want to subject people to these unfortunate working conditions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在任何情况下，我都不想让人们遭受这些不幸的工作条件。

sentences.en: It actually starts at a place where you're like, well, the product's really nice and the shoes look really good on me.
sentences.zh: 它实际上始于这样一个立场：嗯，这产品真的很不错，鞋子穿在我脚上也很好看。

sentences.en: And then you start reasoning about it.
sentences.zh: 然后你开始为此进行辩解。

sentences.en: And that's called motivated reasoning.
sentences.zh: 这被称为动机推理。

sentences.en: So rather than think about morality in terms of this kind of objective thing, we kind of think about it more like a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们不是从这种客观事物的角度来思考道德，而是更像一个律师那样去思考。

sentences.en: So we decide what we want, and then we kind of come up with the reasons to support it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们决定自己想要什么，然后想出各种理由来支持它。

sentences.en: So we may say, oh, if we see a pair of shoes that we don't like, we may say, oh, sweatshop labor is wrong.
sentences.zh: 因此我们可能会说，哦，如果我们看到一双我们不喜欢的鞋子，我们可能会说，哦，血汗工厂的劳工是错误的。

sentences.en: I don't like sweatshop labor.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢血汗工厂的劳工。

sentences.en: I don't approve.
sentences.zh: 我不赞同。

sentences.en: But if the shoes are cute, you might say something like, oh, it's OK because people need jobs or companies need to make money.
sentences.zh: 但如果鞋子很可爱，你可能会说这样的话：哦，这没关系，因为人们需要工作，或者公司需要赚钱。

sentences.en: So you'll be more likely to agree with these things because you're motivated.
sentences.zh: 所以你更有可能赞同这些事情，因为你是有动机的。

sentences.en: In a sense, the shoes are really cute.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，鞋子真的很可爱。

sentences.en: You really want them.
sentences.zh: 你真的很想要它们。

sentences.en: And so you want to find a way to kind of reconcile your kind of distaste for this situation and kind of the reality of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，你想找到一种方法来调和这种对局面的反感与现实状况。

sentences.en: And you've actually conducted experiments which show that people are more likely to reach for these kinds of rationalizations when they actually like a product.
sentences.zh: 你实际上做过实验，结果表明，当人们真正喜欢某个产品时，他们更有可能诉诸这种合理化解释。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: So if they like a product, if you show them sort of an attractive pair of shoes, they'll be more likely to agree with these economic justifications.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们喜欢一个产品，如果你给他们看一双很吸引人的鞋子，他们就会更有可能赞同这些经济上的正当理由。

sentences.en: If you show them an unattractive pair of shoes, all of a sudden they become these kind of moral animals who say, oh, no, it's wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果你给他们看一双并不吸引人的鞋子，他们突然就会变成那种道德动物，说，哦，不，这是不对的。

sentences.en: And so the idea is that we just decide what is moral based on how much we want something.
sentences.zh: 所以这个想法是，我们只是根据我们对某样东西的渴望程度来决定什么是道德的。

sentences.en: One thing you've looked at is that we're often willing to go along with products that are ethically problematic so long as we can come up with a way to distance ourselves from the unethical behavior that produced it.
sentences.zh: 你研究过的一个现象是，只要我们能找到一种方法把自己与产生它的不道德行为拉开距离，我们往往愿意接受存在道德问题的产品。

sentences.en: The more distance we can put between ourselves and the unethical behavior or the unethical action, the easier it becomes to perform.
sentences.zh: 我们与不道德行为或不道德行动拉开的距离越大，这种行为就越容易实施。

sentences.en: So this goes to the idea that if I went to the grocery store and asked for a chicken and they went out and killed a chicken for me,
sentences.zh: 这就好比，如果我去杂货店要一只鸡，然后他们出去为我杀了一只鸡，

sentences.en: I would feel worse about that than if I was just picking up the chicken from a tray.
sentences.zh: 比起我直接从托盘里拿一只鸡，我对这件事的感觉会更糟糕。

sentences.en: And, of course, in both cases, a chicken had to be killed.
sentences.zh: 当然，在这两种情况下，都必须有一只鸡被杀。

sentences.en: But in one case, I feel like I have actually asked for the chicken to be killed.
sentences.zh: 但在一种情况下，我觉得自己实际上要求杀鸡了。

sentences.en: In the other case, the dirty work has already been done.
sentences.zh: 在另一种情况下，脏活已经干完了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's a number of things that sort of enable us to not feel so close to the harm.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多事情让我们感觉没有那么接近伤害。

sentences.en: I mean, essentially, you're buying a product from a company, but what you're doing is you're hiring them to do kind of this dirty work for you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，本质上，你是从一家公司买产品，但你实际上是在雇佣他们为你做这种脏活。

sentences.en: So say any clothing company, they're the ones who hire, you know, a child and maybe, you know, under some unfortunate conditions.
sentences.zh: 比如任何服装公司，他们才是雇佣童工并在某些不幸条件下让他们工作的人。

sentences.en: You're not directly actually hiring that person.
sentences.zh: 你并没有直接去雇佣那个人。

sentences.en: But I think the second thing that happens is this idea of the order of how kind of supply and demand happens.
sentences.zh: 但我认为发生的第二件事是关于供求关系发生顺序的想法。

sentences.en: So we live in an economy where most items are produced firSt.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个大多数商品都是先生产出来的经济体中。

sentences.en: And so they're already produced.
sentences.zh: 所以它们已经生产出来了。

sentences.en: They're already in the store.
sentences.zh: 它们已经在店里了。

sentences.en: And so when you go to the store, the damage has been done, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 所以当你去商店时，可以说是木已成舟。

sentences.en: So it's already been done.
sentences.zh: 所以事情已经做完了。

sentences.en: It's already happened.
sentences.zh: 事情已经发生了。

sentences.en: But imagine that you went into that same store and you had to order your chicken or your clothes on demand.
sentences.zh: 但想象一下，如果你走进同一家商店，你必须按需订购你的鸡肉或衣服。

sentences.en: So if you order it on demand, you know, they then they will put a child, you know, have them work under these unfortunate conditions.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你按需求订购，你知道的，然后他们就会让儿童在这些不幸的条件下工作。

sentences.en: And then you start feeling responsible and guilty for this situation where when it's already happened, you feel like, oh, well,
sentences.zh: 然后你就会开始对这种情况感到责任和内疚，而当事情已经发生时，你会觉得，哦，好吧，

sentences.en: it's already happened and I'm not responsible for it.
sentences.zh: 事情已经发生了，这不怪我。

sentences.en: And I think people don't really kind of see this broader role that consumers have in creating demand for these kinds of products.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们并没有真正看到消费者在为这类产品创造需求方面所扮演的更广泛的角色。

sentences.en: They don't see that A causes B because it sort of happens backwards, that they actually make the product first and then you decide if you want it.
sentences.zh: 他们没有看到A导致了B，因为这有点倒过来发生，即他们实际上先制造产品，然后由你决定是否想要它。

sentences.en: But if we lived in an economy that was all on demand, then it would happen the other way.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们生活在一个完全按需生产的经济体中，情况就会反过来。

sentences.en: You would decide you want it and then they would make it.
sentences.zh: 你会决定你想要它，然后他们才会制造它。

sentences.en: And then there would be a stronger connection,
sentences.zh: 这样就会有更紧密的联系，

sentences.en: kind of a stronger cause and effect connection that I think people would then feel a bit more responsible and a bit more guilty for these kinds of situations.
sentences.zh: 一种更强的因果联系，我认为人们届时会为这类情况感到更多的责任和内疚。

sentences.en: I can imagine that people would feel horrible if they said,
sentences.zh: 我可以想象，如果人们这样说，他们会感到极其糟糕：

sentences.en: I want a shirt and they have to send some poor nine-year-old kid into the basement to make the shirt for the next six hours.
sentences.zh: “我想要一件衬衫”，然后他们必须派一个可怜的九岁小孩去地下室接下来的六个小时里做这件衬衫。

sentences.en: I mean, people would feel awful about that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们对此会感到非常糟糕。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think people wouldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想人们不会那样做的。

sentences.en: And so then it kind of gets to this question of, does the economic structure and the structure of how goods are made,
sentences.zh: 这就引出了这样一个问题：经济结构和货物的制造方式，

sentences.en: does the kind of logistical structure impact how we think about ethics and how we think about our own role in enabling these kinds of harms?
sentences.zh: 这种物流结构是否会影响我们对道德的看法，以及我们如何看待自己在促成这些伤害中所扮演的角色？

sentences.en: The companies who make stuff for us are run by people,
sentences.zh: 为我们制造东西的公司是由人运营的，

sentences.en: and those people have minds that work like our minds.
sentences.zh: 而这些人的思维方式和我们的思维方式是一样的。

sentences.en: So it should come as no surprise that just as consumers would rather have companies do the dirty work for them
sentences.zh: 所以这并不奇怪，正如消费者宁愿让公司替他们干脏活累活

sentences.en: to distance themselves from the ethical consequences of their economic actions,
sentences.zh: 来让自己跟经济行为带来的道德后果保持距离一样，

sentences.en: companies often choose to do exactly the same thing.
sentences.zh: 公司也经常选择这样做。

sentences.en: Rather than run a factory that makes clothing under awful working conditions,
sentences.zh: 与其经营一家在恶劣工作条件下制造服装的工厂，

sentences.en: why not outsource the dirty work to someone else?
sentences.zh: 为什么不把脏活外包给别人呢？

sentences.en: If a reporter unearths details of poor working conditions, you can now plausibly say, but I didn't know about it.
sentences.zh: 如果有记者挖出工作条件恶劣的细节，你现在就可以貌似合理地说，但我对此一无所知啊。

sentences.en: In many cases, companies actually do outsource the harm.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，公司确实把伤害外包了。

sentences.en: So rather than own the factory that makes the clothing under these terrible conditions, we outsource them to other firms that are owned by other entities.
sentences.zh: 因此，与其拥有在这些可怕条件下制造服装的工厂，我们不如将它们外包给其他实体拥有的公司。

sentences.en: So a lot of these companies do try and claim that they had no knowledge of this.
sentences.zh: 所以很多这样的公司确实试图声称他们对此毫不知情。

sentences.en: This did not happen within the boundaries of my firm.
sentences.zh: 这并没有在我的公司范围内发生。

sentences.en: It turns out that both individuals and companies often prefer to be kept in the dark
sentences.zh: 事实证明，个人和公司往往都更愿意被蒙在鼓里，

sentences.en: about unethical practices that are further up the supply chain.
sentences.zh: 不了解供应链上游那些不道德的做法。

sentences.en: So there was a really, really interesting paper by Julie Irwin and some other colleagues
sentences.zh: 朱莉·欧文和一些其他同事曾写过一篇非常非常有趣的文章

sentences.en: who wrote a paper on this idea of willful ignorance.
sentences.zh: 他们写了一篇关于这种刻意无知概念的论文。

sentences.en: And the idea was that you had a product and you had access to a whole bunch of different pieces of information.
sentences.zh: 这个概念是这样的：你拥有一个产品，并且可以获取大量不同的信息。

sentences.en: And one of them was the labor conditions or the environmental conditions.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是劳动条件或环境条件。

sentences.en: And the question was, do people actually ask for this information?
sentences.zh: 问题是，人们真的会去索取这些信息吗？

sentences.en: You can look at it if you want, but you could decide not to look at it.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看的话可以去看，但你也可以决定不看。

sentences.en: And it turns out people didn't want to look at that information because they didn't really want to be confronted with this kind of conflict between their beliefs and what they really wanted.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，人们并不想看这些信息，因为他们真的不想面对这种冲突：一边是他们的信仰，另一边是他们真正想要的东西。

sentences.en: and they found this effect was stronger for people who cared more about labor issues,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，对于那些更关心劳工问题的人来说，这种效应更强，

sentences.en: who cared more about environmental issues.
sentences.zh: 那些更关心环境问题的人也是如此。

sentences.en: They were more likely to avoid, you know, avoid this information in order to kind of avoid this conflict.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能选择逃避，你知道的，逃避这些信息，以此来避免这种冲突。

sentences.en: Think of the deep irony of what Neeru just said.
sentences.zh: 想想尼鲁刚才所说的话中那深层的讽刺。

sentences.en: The folks who care the most about ethics might be most willing to turn a blind eye to unethical business practices
sentences.zh: 那些最关心道德的人可能最愿意对不道德的商业行为视而不见，

sentences.en: because they know if they found out about those practices,
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道，如果他们发现了这些行为，

sentences.en: they would feel obliged to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 他们就会觉得自己有义务做点什么。

sentences.en: We've talked about the many ways in which consumers and companies
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论了消费者和公司之间互相博弈的种种方式，

sentences.en: play games with one another,
sentences.zh: 互相玩着游戏，

sentences.en: using products to speak on their behalf
sentences.zh: 用产品来替自己发声，

sentences.en: or using products behind which they can hide.
sentences.zh: 或者把产品当作藏身之处。

sentences.en: But there's one dimension of economic activity we haven't explored,
sentences.zh: 但经济活动中还有一个我们尚未探讨的维度，

sentences.en: and that's time.
sentences.zh: 那就是时间。

sentences.en: I asked Neeru how some of us use our calendars
sentences.zh: 我问尼鲁，我们当中有些人是如何利用日程表

sentences.en: to broadcast our social status.
sentences.zh: 来宣示我们的社会地位的。

sentences.en: It used to be that people once broadcast their social status
sentences.zh: 过去，人们曾通过无所事事

sentences.en: by being idle.
sentences.zh: 来宣示他们的社会地位。

sentences.en: But that idea has been turned on its head in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但在美国，这个观念已经被彻底颠覆了。

sentences.en: It turns out nowadays that people who are busier actually seem to have more social status.
sentences.zh: 现在的事实是，那些更忙碌的人似乎反而拥有更高的社会地位。

sentences.en: So rather than somebody who is very wealthy, who could waste their time, take fancy vacations,
sentences.zh: 因此，与其像某个非常富有、可以浪费时间、去豪华度假的人那样，

sentences.en: you know, invest in learning these kind of archaic mannerisms,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，投资于学习这种古老繁复的礼仪，

sentences.en: it turns out the person who works really hard, who's really busy, who's very effortful,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，那个工作极其努力、非常忙碌、付出很多努力的人，

sentences.en: is the one who seemed to have more social status, and I think in part that is because we live in a
sentences.zh: 才是似乎拥有更高社会地位的人，我想部分原因是因为我们生活在一个

sentences.en: society that values social mobility.
sentences.zh: 重视社会流动性的社会里。

sentences.en: So we actually conducted the study in the U.S., and we
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上在美国做过这项研究，我们

sentences.en: conducted the same study in Italy, and we found that for Italian people, they thought the person
sentences.zh: 在意大利也做了同样的研究，我们发现对于意大利人来说，他们认为

sentences.en: who was living a life of leisure had more status.
sentences.zh: 过着闲暇生活的人更有地位。

sentences.en: Of course, they have so much money, they can just
sentences.zh: 当然，他们有那么多钱，可以一直

sentences.en: relax all the time, whereas in the U.S., they thought the person who was working all the time
sentences.zh: 放松，而在美国，他们认为整天都在工作的人

sentences.en: actually had more status.
sentences.zh: 实际上更有地位。

sentences.en: And I think what was going on was that in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想当时的情况是，在美国，

sentences.en: people sort of value
sentences.zh: 人们某种程度上珍视

sentences.en: this sense of earned status.
sentences.zh: 这种靠努力换来的地位。

sentences.en: So status can be earned in the U.S., where I think in Italy it's
sentences.zh: 所以在美利坚地位是可以靠努力挣来的，而在意大利我认为

sentences.en: more of a society where status is inherited.
sentences.zh: 那更是一个地位靠世袭的社会。

sentences.en: So for example, my co-author is Italian, and she's
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我的合著者是意大利人，她

sentences.en: always talking about how people come from good families or not.
sentences.zh: 总是在谈论人们是否出身名门。

sentences.en: And so there's very much this
sentences.zh: 因此，这里非常强烈地存在着这样一种

sentences.en: idea that your status isn't necessarily something that you earn, but you inherit.
sentences.zh: 观念：你的地位不一定是你赚来的，而是你继承的。

sentences.en: And so in that
sentences.zh: 所以在那种

sentences.en: sense, working hard really wouldn't get you anywhere.
sentences.zh: 意义上，努力工作确实不会让你有所成就。

sentences.en: Whereas in America, you have the
sentences.zh: 而在美国，你会有一种

sentences.en: sense that you can actually climb the ladder.
sentences.zh: 感觉，觉得你确实可以往上爬。

sentences.en: And so celebrities, for example, might say,
sentences.zh: 所以，比如名人们可能会说，

sentences.en: instead of saying, you know, I make one movie every year, and I get to hang out on the beach
sentences.zh: 他们不会说，你知道的，我每年拍一部电影，剩下的10个月都在海滩上闲逛

sentences.en: for the other 10 months of the year, they actually are suggesting, oh, my God, I'm so overworked.
sentences.zh: 而是暗示，噢天哪，我工作实在太多了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So we actually looked at tweets of celebrities who were tagged with this
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上查看了被贴上

sentences.en: hashtag humblebrag, this idea of bragging, but sort of disguising it as a complaint.
sentences.zh: 微型炫耀（humblebrag）标签的名人推文，这种炫耀的概念是，假装在抱怨，实则在炫耀。

sentences.en: And a lot of the ones, a lot of the tweets we found had to do with being busy.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的许多推文都与忙碌有关。

sentences.en: So, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，

sentences.en: I have to be in the recording studio this morning, and then I have a book meeting in the afternoon,
sentences.zh: 我今天早上得去录音室，然后下午有个图书会议，

sentences.en: and then I have to travel to New York in the evening, and hashtag I have no life, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后晚上还得去纽约，话题标签：我没有生活了，你知道的，

sentences.en: these kinds of tweets.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的推文。

sentences.en: You're trying to say something about yourself.
sentences.zh: 你是在试图表达关于你自己的某些信息。

sentences.en: You're busy.
sentences.zh: 你很忙。

sentences.en: You're
sentences.zh: 你

sentences.en: really important.
sentences.zh: 非常重要。

sentences.en: You don't have time to do other things.
sentences.zh: 你没有时间去做别的事。

sentences.en: And so you see that on social media,
sentences.zh: 所以你在社交媒体上会看到这一点，

sentences.en: that's kind of an acceptable and effective way to show your status by telling people how busy you
sentences.zh: 这算是一种被接受且有效的方式，通过告诉别人你有多忙来展示你的

sentences.en: are.
sentences.zh: 地位。
